title.narrative: Women and Girl safe spaces: Protection, education, vocational training and grants

description.narrative:
WND/SMK project will provide protection, education, small business training, and digital literacy programs for women and girls in Mare’a. These activities aim to enhance economic empowerment, psychosocial resilience, and access to specialised services for vulnerable women and girls while fostering community engagement and skill-building. * ​​Protection and Psychosocial Support (PSS)​ main activities​:​​​ ​​​Awareness informative sessions on a variety of topics related to their daily lives.​​ ​​​Structured Group PSS and health sessions include two main programmes:​​ - Women's Program includes PSS Group & Health Awareness Sessions (Structured).​​ ​​​- Girls' Program includes PSS Group & Health Awareness Sessions (Structured).​​ ​​​Young Mothers Club​​ will provide targeted support for adolescent mothers, focusing on family planning, child development, and emotional support. ​​​Focused parenting support.​​ women will receive parenting skills training to improve their ability to manage child behaviour and family stress. ​​​Specialized Protection services: One-to-one PSS consultation and GBV Case Management.​​ ​​​Cash for protection support.​​ ​​First Aid Course.​​​ The training sessions will target women to provide skills in dealing with emergency situations like wounds, burns, scorpion stings and others that need immediate response.​ ​​​Child care/ Nursery for the staff and the participants’ children.​​​​ * Education and Skills Development​:​ ​​SMK will enhance women’s and girls’ access to education by providing Arabic literacy and Quran recitation courses, which have strong local acceptance​ and encourage the parents to send their daughter to attend the courses​.​​​ Additionally, complementary education courses will be offered, targeting adolescent girls preparing for public exams (for 9th and 12th grade) in subjects such as physics, mathematics, chemistry, and Arabic. * Vocational and Economic Empowerment To promote financial independence, women and girls will have small business training that ends up with small grants. Graduates of previous SMK vocational programs will have access to entrepreneurship training and mini-grants, enabling them to launch small businesses. Each entrepreneurial group will receive 1000$ grant, along with mentoring sessions to support long-term sustainability. * Digital Literacy and Technology Access.
Project location: Mare’a Sub-District, Azaz District, Aleppo Governorate, Northern Syria (Location).
